Consider the polyhedron defined by the set {x : Ax ≤b}. If F is a minimal face
of this polyhedron, demonstrate that Ax = Ay for every pair of points x, y ∈F.
Definition 1. Let P = {x : Ax ≤b} be a polyhedron where A ∈Rm×n and b ∈Rm. A face
of P is a set of the form
F = {x ∈P : aT
i x = bi for all i ∈I}
for some index set I ⊆{1, . . . , m}, where aT
i denotes the i-th row of A.
A face is minimal (or an extreme face) if it contains no other proper faces, i.e., if
F ′ ⊆F is a face, then either F ′ = ∅or F ′ = F.
Theorem 1. If F is a minimal face of the polyhedron P = {x : Ax ≤b}, then Ax = Ay for
every pair of points x, y ∈F.
Proof. We first establish a key characterization of minimal faces.

F is convex and contains x, y, we have [x, y] ⊆F.

This proves that Ax = Ay for every pair of points x, y ∈F.
Alternative formulation: The result can also be understood as follows: A minimal
face consists of a single point, which is uniquely determined by the active constraints. At
this vertex v, all constraints achieve specific values: for the active constraints (those in index
set I), we have aT
i v = bi, and for inactive constraints, we have aT
i v < bi. Since there is only
one point in F, the vector Av is uniquely determined, making Ax = Ay = Av for all x, y ∈F
(as they are all equal to v).
